proofs.proof_tex:
By \texttt{def:target},
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \left\{\mathbb E[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]
             -\mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency} gives
\(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\) almost surely.  Equality almost surely
therefore implies, for the conditional expectations already appearing in
\texttt{def:target},
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]
 =\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\tag{2}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-date-transport} separately gives
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]=m_s(z_{0s}).
\tag{3}
\]
Substituting (2)--(3) into the finite sum (1) proves
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \left\{\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\right\}.
\]
Thus the observed-law functional is derived from the causal contrast; it is
not the definition of that contrast.  No regression, overlap, mixing, donor,
or rank condition is used in this identification step.

Put
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda.
\tag{1}
\]
We first work solely in the deterministic experiment
\(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\).  Fix
\(\xi=(\mathbb Q_\xi;\mu,f,z)\).  Conditional on the donor sample, define
for each unit
\[
 U_{si}=E_{si}-\mu_s-K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \{Q_{s,t_{s\ell},i}-f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})\}.
\tag{2}
\]
The donor sample is independent of the sigma-field generated by all unit
histories in \texttt{def:fixed-design-induced-experiment}; hence conditioning
on the donor-selected indices does not change either displayed mean.
Therefore \(\mathbb E(U_{si}\mid(Z_j)_j)=0\).  The unit histories are
independent across \((s,i)\), so the variables in (2) are independent across
\((s,i)\) under the same conditioning.  Bounded support and
\(\|f_s\|_\infty\vee|\mu_s|\le B\) give \(|U_{si}|\le4B\).  Thus
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\left(
 \sum_s\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\sum_iU_{si}
 \mathrel{\Big|}(Z_j)_j\right)\le16B^2A.
\tag{3}
\]

Let \(t_s^0\) be a nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\).  Nearest-neighbor
optimality and the triangle inequality give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|X_{s,t_{s\ell}}-z_s\|_2
 &\le \|X_{s,t_s^0}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2
       +\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2\\
 &\le \rho_{sX}(z_{0s})+\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2
       +2\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
For \(0<\lambda\le1\), subadditivity of \(x^\lambda\) and Holder
continuity imply
\[
 |f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})-f_s(z_s)|
 \le C\{\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda+
 \|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda+
 \|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2^\lambda\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Projection onto the cube is nonexpansive, every balanced fold has
\(|I_\ell|\ge N/3\), and the donor covariance restriction gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\|\widetilde z_\ell-z\|_2^2
 \le\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}{|I_\ell|}
 \le\frac{3SdC_\Sigma}{N}.
\tag{6}
\]
The local parameter restriction also gives
\(\|z-z_0\|_2^2\le C_\Sigma/N\).  Jensen's inequality, (3)--(6), and
the finite weighted sum therefore yield
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \le C\{A+D_X^2+N^{-\lambda}\}
 \le CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}},
\tag{7}
\]
where the last comparison is
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry}.  The first minimax
inequality follows because \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}\) is one admissible
data-measurable estimator.

For the converse, we first record an elementary two-law inequality.  If laws
\(P_0,P_1\) have targets separated by \(\Delta\) and
\(\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1-\eta\), then, with
\(A_0=\{|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0|<\Delta/2\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v(\widetilde\theta-\theta_v)^2
 &\ge\frac{\Delta^2}{8}\{P_0(A_0^c)+P_1(A_0)\}\\
 &\ge\frac{\eta\Delta^2}{8}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
The first line follows by considering the error under the appropriate law on
each event, and the second is the variational definition of total variation.

For the treated-mean channel, fix the response and donor coordinates and,
under \(v\in\{-1,1\}\), take independent
\(E_{si}\in\{-b,b\}\), where \(0<b<B\), with
\[
 \Pr_v(E_{si}=b)=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.
\tag{9}
\]
Since \(A\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), a fixed sufficiently small \(\gamma\) makes
all probabilities lie in \([1/4,3/4]\).  The target separation is
\(4\gamma\sqrt A\).  The Hellinger affinity between the product laws is
\[
 \prod_s(1-4\varepsilon_s^2)^{n_s/2}
 \ge\exp(-C\gamma^2/b^2)>0.
\tag{10}
\]
The Cauchy--Schwarz relation between affinity and total variation used in
\texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} and (8) give risk at least
\(cA\).

For the fixed-design channel, use the functions \(f_s=q_s/2\) and
\(g_s=-q_s/2\) constructed in
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry}.  They agree at every
design site.  Taking deterministic responses equal to those common site
values and identical donor and event laws makes the observed laws identical,
while their targets differ by \(aD_X\).  Equation (8) gives risk at least
\(cD_X^2\).

For the donor channel, the construction of
\texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} is transported to the prescribed
\(\Sigma\) as follows.  Choose a coordinate vector \(e\) in a cohort and a
sign such that a small displacement remains in the trimmed cube, and put
\(w=\Sigma^{-1/2}e/\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2\).  Rotate the standardized
three-point first coordinate onto \(w\), and transform it by
\(\Sigma^{1/2}\).  At parameters zero and \(c_*N^{-1/2}\), the two donor
means are
\[
 z_0,\qquad
 z_0+\frac{c_*N^{-1/2}}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}e.
\tag{11}
\]
Their covariance is exactly \(\Sigma\), their standardized fourth moments
remain below \(B^4\) by the strict slack, and their squared standardized mean
separation is \(c_*^2/N\).  The Hellinger calculation in that lemma is
unchanged by the invertible rotation and linear map, so their total variation
is at most \(1-\eta_0\) for small fixed \(c_*\).  Because
\(c_\Sigma I\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I\), the Euclidean displacement
in (11) is comparable to \(N^{-1/2}\).  A common affine surface for
\(\lambda=1\), or a common one-sided \(\lambda\)-cusp for
\(0<\lambda<1\), separates the targets by \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\).  The
response and event laws are identical.  Equation (8) gives risk at least
\(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Taking the maximum of the three channel bounds and using
the two-sided characterization in
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} proves the deterministic
lower bound.  The strict conditions \(\delta_0<1/2\) and
\(B^4>(Sd)^2\) are used only in this regular donor construction.

We next establish the causal bridge.  Let
\(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{st})_{s,t})\), let \(\mathcal H\) be the
sigma-field generated by all unit training and event histories, and let
\(\mathcal Z=\sigma((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  The clarified
\texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} states
\(\mathcal Z\perp\!\!\!\perp(\mathcal X\vee\mathcal H)\mid z_0\).
Therefore, for every bounded \(\mathcal Z\)-measurable random variable \(U\)
and bounded \(\mathcal H\)-measurable random variable \(V\),
\[
 \mathbb E(UV\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 =\mathbb E(U\mid z_0)\mathbb E(V\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
\tag{12}
\]
almost surely.  Thus conditioning further on \(X\) preserves both the donor
i.i.d. law and its independence from the complete collection of unit
histories.  Together with design-conditional centering, conditional
cross-unit independence, boundedness, and the donor moment restrictions,
(12) shows that the observed regular conditional kernel, with its induced
labels, is an element of \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) for
\(P\)-almost every \(X\).  No kernel is selected at a null design.
By \texttt{lem:causal-identification}, its statistical target equals
\(\tau(z_0)\).  Applying (7) to this almost-sure kernel proves the asserted
causal conditional upper bound.

If each cohort contains \(z_{0s}\) exactly, then \(D_X=0\), and the
exact-site conclusion follows from the geometry lemma.  Finally suppose
\(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every cohort.  Then
\((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) is feasible in every anchor search.  Selected-certificate
optimality gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &C_H\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s\widehat h_{s\ell}^d)^{-1/2}\\
 &\quad\le C_H\|z_{0s}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d)^{-1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]
The bandwidth floor makes the final variance certificate at most
\((h_s^\star)^\lambda\).  Because \(r=0\), the fitted weights are
nonnegative and sum to one.  Holder continuity bounds their conditional bias
by the first two terms on the left of (13), while conditional cross-unit
independence bounds their stochastic variance by \(C/n_s\).  Equation (6),
Jensen's inequality, and (13) therefore imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\{\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0,X]
 \le CR_D.
\tag{14}
\]
The geometry lemma separately gives \(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D\).
No reverse comparison with the Gram certificate is used or asserted.

Put
\[
 A=\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad D_T=\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{2\lambda/d}.
\tag{1}
\]
Whenever the attained anchor at \(z_0\) is coercive, the proof of
\texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} applies with the comparison pair
\((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\); this includes a genuinely attained top bandwidth
equal to one.  If no such comparison pair exists, the fixed-scale occupancy
argument in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} gives probability at
most \(CT^{-2}\), and clipping bounds squared error by \(16B^2\).  Averaging
the conditional bound over the exact design and applying the two moment
bounds of that lemma yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P[\{\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0]
 \le C\bigg[&A+
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2\\
 &+D_T+N^{-\lambda}\bigg]
 \le CR_\star.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
The term \(CT^{-2}\) is absorbed by \(D_T\).

The displayed smoothing term is redundant.  With
\(a_s=n_s^{-1/2}\) and \(b=T^{-\lambda/d}\),
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =a_s^{2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}b^{d/(2\lambda+d)}
 \le a_s\vee b.
\tag{3}
\]
Since \(S\) is fixed, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2
 \le2S\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}+2T^{-2\lambda/d}
 \le C(A+D_T).
\tag{4}
\]

Assume now \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\).  The elementary
two-law bound (8) in the proof of \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} applies
to every embedded subexperiment.  For the treated-mean channel, translate
the two-point outcomes in (9) of that proof into a fixed subinterval of
\((0,B)\), use independent uniform designs, a common admissible donor law,
and constant untreated surfaces.  Set the treated potential wealth equal to
the translated observed outcome and the untreated potential wealth equal to
the constant surface.  Taking \(W_{si,-1}=1\), the horizon-zero return equal
to wealth minus one, and all later returns zero verifies
\texttt{def:buyhold-level}.  The donor sample is independent of the entire
joint panel.  This embeds the product experiment in the causal model and
gives risk at least \(cA\).

Lemma \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} supplies two base-class
laws with risk lower bound \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  For any fixed auxiliary
error probability in \((0,1/2)\), lemma
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies two laws with
a common subprobability measure of positive mass and target separation
\(cD_T^{1/2}\), and hence risk at least \(cD_T\).  Taking the largest of
these three lower bounds and using (4) proves the marginal minimax
equivalence.

On the independent-calendar subclass, the independent version of
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} replaces \(D_T\) by
\(T^{-2\lambda/d}\) in the upper bound.  For the converse, take a ball of
radius \(r_T=cT^{-1/d}\) around \(z_{01}\) and two Holder regressions
that agree off the ball and differ at its center by \(c_1r_T^\lambda\).
The density upper bound gives hit probability at most
\(C_Xv_dr_T^d\) per design point.  For small fixed \(c\), independence
therefore gives
\[
 \Pr\{X_{1t}\text{ misses the ball for all }t\}
 =(1-p_T)^T\ge c_2>0.
\tag{5}
\]
On this event the two observed regression laws coincide, while their targets
differ by \(c_1T^{-\lambda/d}\); the two-law inequality gives the matching
squared-risk lower bound.  Finally, setting \(S=1\), \(d=1\), and
\(n_1=n\) in (2) gives the scalar bookkeeping display, and (4) proves that
its smoothing term is dominated.

By \texttt{lem:causal-identification}, the target equals the displayed
observed-law functional and, by bounded wealth, lies in \([-2B,2B]\).  We
first prove coverage on the regular branch.  Conditional on the exact design
and donor sample, the selected local-constant weights are response-independent.
For each \((s,i)\), form the centered contrast
\[
 \xi_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\left[
 B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0)
 -\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_{st}\{Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\}\right].
\tag{1}
\]
The clarified donor--panel factorization implies that further conditioning on
the donor sample does not change the conditional laws of any unit history.
Thus \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} centers (1), and
\texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} makes the \(\xi_{si}\) independent
across \((s,i)\).  Its range length is at most
\[
 \frac{2B\pi_s}{n_s}\left(1+\sum_t|w_{st}|\right).
\]
For any \(V\in[a,b]\), convexity of the exponential and exponential Markov
give
\[
 \mathbb E e^{u(V-\mathbb EV)}\le e^{u^2(b-a)^2/8}.
\tag{2}
\]
Applying (2) to the independent sum shows that the two-sided sampling error
exceeds \(r_{\mathrm{unit}}\) with probability at most
\[
 2\exp\{-4\log(8/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}})\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/4.
\]
The added linear bounded-range term only enlarges this valid radius and no
variance estimate is inverted.

For the calendar construction, each retained score block is excluded from
the response data used by its cross-fit.  Successively replacing the retained
blocks within each parity by independent copies changes the joint law, in
total variation, by at most
\(2SK_T\beta_0\rho_0^{a_T}\); this follows by telescoping the defining
absolute-regularity bounds.  Conditional on the cross-fit sigma-field, block
\(k\) has range at most \(L_k\).  Applying (2) to the independent comparison
blocks in the two parities, adding the deterministic discarded-index bound
\(L_{\mathcal G}\) gives a response-score failure probability at most
\(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/2\) by the scalar defining inequality for
\(x_{\mathrm{cal}}\).  A separate application of (2) to the treated
replicates gives
\[
 \Pr\{|\text{treated-mean error}|>r_B\mid z_0\}
 \le 2\exp\{-4\log(16/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}})\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/4.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \Pr\{\text{sampling error}>r_{\mathrm{cal}}\mid z_0\}
 \le3\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/4.
\tag{3}
\]
Since \(r_{\mathrm{samp}}=r_{\mathrm{unit}}\wedge r_{\mathrm{cal}}\), the event
that the error exceeds \(r_{\mathrm{samp}}\) is contained in the union of
the two error events just bounded.  Its probability is therefore at most
\(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}\).

For the donor radius, spectral clipping gives
\(\widehat\Sigma\succeq(c_\Sigma/2)I\).  Projection is nonexpansive,
\(|I_\ell|\ge N/3\), and donor unbiasedness and ellipticity imply
\[
 \mathbb E\left[N\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}
 (\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2^2\mid z_0\right]
 \le\frac{6SdC_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma}.
\tag{4}
\]
Markov's inequality and a union bound over at most two folds, with the stated
\(q_{\mathrm{don}}\), yield
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_\ell
 \|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2
 >q_{\mathrm{don}}N^{-1/2}\mid z_0\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{5}
\]
On the complement of (5), the upper spectral clipping bound converts this
Mahalanobis radius into a Euclidean radius of order \(N^{-1/2}\).  Holder
continuity, the local-constant bias calculation, and the selected-certificate
inequality then bound the deterministic error by
\(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Combining (3)--(5) with
\(\alpha=\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\) proves coverage on
the regular branch.  On every declared bad branch the interval is
\([-2B,2B]\), which contains the target, so coverage there is one.

We next bound expected length.  Since \(r=0\), every regular response weight
is nonnegative and \(\sum_t|w_{st}|=1\).  Hence
\[
 r_{\mathrm{unit}}\le C(\alpha,B)A^{1/2},
 \qquad r_{\mathrm{samp}}\le r_{\mathrm{unit}}.
\tag{6}
\]
Whenever the anchor comparison at \(z_0\) is available, selected-certificate
optimality and the bandwidth floor give
\[
 r_{\mathrm{bias}}
 \le C\sum_s\pi_s\left\{(h_s^\star)^\lambda+
 K_N^{-1}\sum_\ell\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\right\}.
\tag{7}
\]
Donor unbiasedness, ellipticity, projection nonexpansiveness, and Jensen's
inequality give
\(\mathbb E\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\le CN^{-\lambda/2}\).
Taking expectations in (7) and using
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\mid z_0)
 \le C\bigg[&\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 +\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}
 +N^{-\lambda/2}\bigg].
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
Along the stated growth arrays, every deterministic small-sample branch
eventually disappears.  The fixed-scale occupancy proof in the anchor-moment
lemma bounds the remaining missing-anchor contribution by \(CT^{-2}\).
Equations (6)--(8) and the smoothing domination proved in
\texttt{thm:marginal-phase-diagram} yield the expected-length upper bound.
Under calendar independence, the anchor-moment lemma replaces the logarithmic
term by \(T^{-\lambda/d}\).

For the converse, suppose two laws with targets \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) share
a common subprobability measure \(\nu\) of mass \(\eta>2\alpha\).  Uniform
coverage \(1-\alpha-o(1)\) under both laws implies
\[
 \nu\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I_\alpha\}
 \ge\eta-2\alpha-o(1).
\]
Therefore
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)
 \ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\{\eta-2\alpha-o(1)\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Choose the treated two-point displacement in the conditional proof small
enough that its Hellinger common mass exceeds \(2\alpha\); (9) gives
\(c_\alpha A^{1/2}\).  Under the strict moment and interior slack, the
standardized displacement multiplier in
\texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} can likewise be chosen small,
giving common mass above \(2\alpha\) and separation
\(c_\alpha N^{-\lambda/2}\).  The rare-cluster lemma supplies common mass
above \(2\alpha\) and separation
\(c_\alpha\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{\lambda/d}\).  The independent-calendar
no-hit construction in the marginal proof supplies its
\(T^{-\lambda/d}\) analogue.  Taking the largest channel and using the
smoothing domination proves the stated expected-length lower bounds.

Let \(q=Sd\) and \(\Delta_B=B^4-q^2>0\).  Choose \(a_D>1\) so that
\[
 1<a_D^2<1+\Delta_B/2.
\tag{1}
\]
For \(|u|\) in a sufficiently small fixed neighborhood of zero, define
\(V_u\) on \(\{-a_D,0,a_D\}\) by
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}+\frac{u}{2a_D},\qquad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}-\frac{u}{2a_D},\qquad
 p_0(u)=1-\frac{1+u^2}{a_D^2}.
\tag{2}
\]
All three probabilities are then positive.  Direct summation gives
\[
 \mathbb EV_u=u,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(V_u)=1.
\tag{3}
\]
Let the other \(q-1\) coordinates be independent Rademacher variables.
At \(u=0\),
\[
 \mathbb E\|V_0^{(q)}\|_2^4
 =a_D^2+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2=q^2-1+a_D^2<B^4.
\tag{4}
\]
The centered fourth moment is continuous in \(u\), so the strict inequality
persists on a smaller fixed neighborhood.

Put \(z^{(0)}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_q\) and
\(z^{(1)}=z^{(0)}+\delta_Ne_1\), where
\(\delta_N=c_*N^{-1/2}\).  Since \(\delta_0<1/2\), both paths meet the
interior condition for all sufficiently large \(N\).  Under alternative
\(v\in\{0,1\}\), use i.i.d. donors whose first coordinate is
\(1/2+V_{v\delta_N}\) and whose remaining coordinates are \(1/2\) plus
the common Rademacher coordinates.  Then (3)--(4) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_vZ_j=z^{(v)},\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_v(Z_j)=I_q,\qquad
 \mathbb E_v\|Z_j-z^{(v)}\|_2^4\le B^4.
\tag{5}
\]
Because \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), this verifies the full covariance
ellipticity condition.

The square roots of the three strictly positive probabilities in (2) have
bounded derivatives near zero.  The mean-value theorem therefore gives a
constant \(C_0\) such that the one-donor squared Hellinger distance between
parameters zero and \(\delta_N\) is at most \(C_0\delta_N^2\).  If
\(A(P,Q)=\int\sqrt{dP\,dQ}\) denotes Hellinger affinity, product
factorization gives
\(A(P_0^{Z,N},P_1^{Z,N})\ge(1-C_0\delta_N^2)^N\).  Moreover,
Cauchy--Schwarz applied to
\(|p-q|=|\sqrt p-\sqrt q|(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)\) gives
\[
 \|P-Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\{1-A(P,Q)^2\}^{1/2}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \|P_1^{Z,N}-P_0^{Z,N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\left\{1-(1-C_0\delta_N^2)^{2N}\right\}^{1/2}.
\tag{6}
\]
Choosing the fixed \(c_*>0\) sufficiently small makes (6) at most
\(1-\eta_0\) for a fixed \(\eta_0>0\).

Use a common i.i.d. uniform exact training design.  If
\(0<\kappa<1\), set
\[
 m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)_+^\kappa;
\]
if \(\kappa=1\), set
\(m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)\).  Set all other surfaces equal to
\(b_0\).  Fixed positive \(b_0,b_1\), chosen sufficiently small in terms
of \(B,L\), put these surfaces in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), keep
them strictly inside \([-B,B]\), and give
\[
 |m_1(z^{(1)}_1)-m_1(z^{(0)}_1)|=b_1\delta_N^\kappa.
\tag{7}
\]
Take the same bounded centered response noise, the same training design, and
the same positive constant treated observations under both alternatives.
Thus the complete observed joint panel law is identical under the two laws.
Set \(B_{si}(1)=B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and set the unobserved untreated
event wealth to the constant \(m_s(z_s^{(v)})\).  All amplitudes may be
chosen in \((0,B)\).  With \(W_{si,-1}=1\),
\(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\), and \(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\),
\texttt{def:buyhold-level} reproduces these wealth levels.  The product
construction verifies consistency, transport, boundedness, conditional
centering, cross-unit independence, and geometric mixing.  It also makes the
donor sample conditionally independent of the entire joint panel
\(((X_{st},Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i})\), which is the
clarified \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}; donor i.i.d. sampling,
unbiasedness, ellipticity, and the fourth-moment condition follow from (5).

By \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (7), the target separation is
\[
 |\tau_1(z^{(1)})-\tau_0(z^{(0)})|
 =\pi_1b_1c_*^\kappa N^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{8}
\]
The panel laws are identical and (6) controls the only differing observed
factor, so (6)--(8) prove the asserted two-law certificate without a
class-wide lower-modulus assumption.

Let \(q=Sd\).  The condition \(B^4\ge q^2\) permits a common donor law
\(Z_j=z_0+U_j\), where the coordinates of \(U_j\) are independent
Rademacher variables.  This law has mean \(z_0\), covariance \(I_q\), and
standardized fourth moment \(q^2\), and we take it independent of the entire
joint panel.

Choose \(\gamma>0\) so small that \(e^{-\gamma}>2\alpha\), and put
\[
 L_T=\left\lfloor
 \frac{\log T-2\log\log(T\vee3)}{|\log\rho_0|}
 \right\rfloor\vee1,
 \qquad p_T=\frac{\gamma L_T}{T}.
\tag{1}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\),
\[
 2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}.
\tag{2}
\]
Partition the first cohort's calendar into consecutive complete blocks of
length \(L_T\).  Independently label each complete block by
\(C_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Let \(A_T\) be a cube centered
at \(z_{01}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_d\) with volume \(p_T\).  Conditional on
\(C_b=1\), draw every point in block \(b\) independently uniformly on
\(A_T\); conditional on \(C_b=0\), draw them independently uniformly on
its complement.  At each complete-block time the marginal density is exactly
\[
 p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
 +(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1.
\tag{3}
\]
Draw the incomplete block and all other cohorts independently and uniformly.

If \(k<L_T\), past and future sigma-fields separated by \(k\) indices can
share at most one block label.  In the total-variation definition of the
absolute-regularity coefficient, replacing that Bernoulli label by an
independent copy changes the joint law by at most \(2p_T\).  If
\(k\ge L_T\), the sigma-fields use disjoint labels and are independent.
Thus (2) yields, for all \(k\ge1\),
\[
 \beta(k)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k.
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(E_T\) be the event that all complete block labels vanish and that no
point in the incomplete block falls in a fixed smaller concentric cube.
The incomplete-block failure probability is at most
\(L_Tp_T=o(1)\), whereas
\[
 \Pr(E_T)=(1-p_T)^{\lfloor T/L_T\rfloor}-o(1)
 \longrightarrow e^{-\gamma}>
 \eta_\alpha:=\frac{e^{-\gamma}+2\alpha}{2}>2\alpha.
\tag{5}
\]
Let \(h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}\) be the side scale of the smaller cube, and
choose a fixed smooth bump \(\phi\), supported inside that cube after
rescaling, with \(\phi(0)=1\).  For a sufficiently small fixed \(a>0\),
define
\[
 m_{10}(x)=b_0,\qquad
 m_{11}(x)=b_0+ah_T^\lambda
 \phi((x-z_{01})/h_T),
\tag{6}
\]
and keep all other surfaces equal to \(b_0\).  The derivative scaling of
the bump makes its \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) norm bounded uniformly in
\(T\); choosing \(a,b_0\) small enforces the Holder radius and bounded
wealth.

Under alternative \(v\), set
\(Q_{1ti}=m_{1v}(X_{1t})\), use the common constant surfaces elsewhere,
keep positive treated observations identical, impose consistency, and set
the unobserved untreated event wealth equal to \(m_{sv}(z_{0s})\).  The
same one-period-return construction as in \texttt{def:buyhold-level}
realizes these positive wealth levels.  Conditional centering and transport
hold by construction; conditional-on-design unit histories are degenerate
and hence mutually independent.  The donor law is independent of the entire
joint panel, and the joint design--response sequence inherits (4).

On \(E_T\), no observed response is evaluated in the bump support.  The
restrictions of the two observed laws to \(E_T\) therefore coincide, so
they possess a common subprobability measure of mass at least
\(\eta_\alpha\) for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Finally,
\texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (6) give
\[
 |\tau_1(z_0)-\tau_0(z_0)|
 =\pi_1ah_T^\lambda
 \asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
\tag{7}
\]
This proves the certificate directly in the base Holder class.

Because \(0<\lambda\le1\), the order convention gives \(r=0\), so the
local-polynomial Gram matrix is scalar.  Continuity of \(K\) and its strict
positivity on a smaller ball provide \(k_0>0\) and \(\eta\in(0,1)\) such
that \(K(v)\ge k_0\) for \(\|v\|_2\le\eta\).  Interiority and the
conditional design-density lower bound give, for
\(b\le\delta_0/\eta\),
\[
 p_b:=\Pr\{\|X_{st}-z_{0s}\|_2\le\eta b\mid z_0\}
 \ge c_Xv_d\eta^db^d=:c_pb^d.
\tag{1}
\]
If \(M_b\) counts these visits, then
\[
 G_{sT}(z_{0s},b)\ge\frac{k_0M_b}{Tb^d}.
\tag{2}
\]

Divide the calendar into consecutive blocks of length \(a_T\), and split
the complete blocks by parity.  Blocks in either parity are separated by at
least \(a_T\) observations.  From the total-variation definition of
absolute regularity, successively replacing those retained blocks by
independent blocks changes the expectation of any function bounded by one by
at most the sum of the intervening beta coefficients.  A telescoping sum over
the two parities is bounded by
\[
 2\left\lceil\frac{T}{a_T}\right\rceil
 \beta_0\rho_0^{a_T}\le CT^{-2},
\tag{3}
\]
because \(\rho_0^{a_T}\le(T\vee2)^{-3}\).

For an independent retained-block count \(Y_j\in[0,a_T]\), convexity of
\(y\mapsto e^{-y/a_T}\) on this interval gives
\[
 \mathbb E(e^{-Y_j/a_T})
 \le1-\frac{1-e^{-1}}{a_T}\mathbb E(Y_j)
 \le\exp\left\{-\frac{1-e^{-1}}{a_T}\mathbb E(Y_j)\right\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Exponential Markov applied to the independent comparison blocks, separately
for the two parities, and then (1), (3), and (4), yield constants
\(c_1,C_1>0\) such that, whenever \(Tb^d\ge C_1a_T\),
\[
 \Pr\{M_b\le c_1Tb^d\mid z_0\}
 \le C_1\exp\{-c_1Tb^d/a_T\}+C_1T^{-2}.
\tag{5}
\]
For smaller \(Tb^d/a_T\), the bound is made trivial by increasing
\(C_1\).  The prescribed compatibility of \(c_G\) with the population
local-constant Gram lower bound makes the right side of (2) at least
\(c_G\) on the complement of the event in (5).

Set
\[
 b_\circ=(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}
 \vee N^{-1/2}\vee(a_T/T)^{1/d}.
\tag{6}
\]
At each dyadic scale not below a constant multiple of
\(2^qb_\circ\), (5) and a union bound over the remaining dyadic candidates
give
\[
 \Pr\{h_s^\star>C2^qb_\circ\mid z_0\}
 \le C\exp(-c2^{qd})+CT^{-2}.
\tag{7}
\]
If the scale exceeds one the assertion is trivial because
\(h_s^\star\le1\).  Integrating the dyadic tail gives
\[
 \mathbb E[(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}\mid z_0]
 \le Cb_\circ^{2\lambda}+CT^{-2}.
\tag{8}
\]
Since \(a_T\asymp\log(T\vee2)\) and \(2\lambda/d\le2\), (8) is
\[
 \mathbb E[(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}\mid z_0]
 \le C\left\{(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}+N^{-\lambda}
 +\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right)^{2\lambda/d}\right\}.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives the corresponding bound for the first moment of
\((h_s^\star)^\lambda\).

At \(b=1\), the intersection of the fixed positivity ball of \(K\) with
the cube has volume bounded below uniformly in the center.  Repeating
(1)--(5) at this fixed scale shows that failure of every coercive candidate
has probability at most \(CT^{-2}\).  A union bound over the fixed number
\(SK_N\) of fold--cohort searches proves
\(\Pr(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\mid z_0)\le CT^{-2}\).  Under calendar
independence the product comparison is exact and one may take \(a_T=1\);
the last term in (8) is then \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).

Write
\[
 \rho_s=\rho_{sX}(z_{0s}),\qquad
 D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_s^\lambda,
 \qquad A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}.
\tag{1}
\]
Take a feasible triple \((f,g,z)\) in
\texttt{def:joint-product-modulus} and put \(q_s=f_s-g_s\).  If
\(t_s\) is a nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\), the response part of
the testing budget is nonnegative cohort by cohort and hence
\[
 |q_s(X_{s t_s})|^2
 \le \sum_{t=1}^{T}|q_s(X_{st})|^2\le n_s^{-1}.
\tag{2}
\]
The difference of two members of \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) is
\(\lambda\)-Holder with constant at most \(2L\).  Since
\(0<\lambda\le1\), (2) and the definition of \(\rho_s\) imply
\[
 |q_s(z_{0s})|\le n_s^{-1/2}+2L\rho_s^\lambda.
\tag{3}
\]
The donor part of the same testing budget and
\(\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\) give
\[
 \|z-z_0\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(z-z_0)\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}N^{-1/2}.
\tag{4}
\]
Splitting the functional difference, applying (3)--(4), and using
\(\sum_s\pi_s=1\) and Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\mathcal T(f,z_0)-\mathcal T(g,z)|
 &\le \sum_s\pi_s|q_s(z_{0s})|
       +L\sum_s\pi_s\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda\\
 &\le C\{A^{1/2}+D_X+N^{-\lambda/2}\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
Indeed, \(\sum_s\pi_sn_s^{-1/2}\le S^{1/2}A^{1/2}\), and \(S\) is
fixed.  Taking the supremum proves the required upper bound for
\(\Omega_X\).  The same argument with one cohort and no donor displacement
proves
\[
 \omega_{s,X}(1;z_{0s})
 \le n_s^{-1/2}+2L\rho_s^\lambda.
\tag{6}
\]

For the fixed-design lower bound, let
\(\mathcal X_s=\{X_{s1},\ldots,X_{sT}\}\) and define
\[
 q_s(x)=a\,\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal X_s)^\lambda,
\tag{7}
\]
where \(a>0\) is chosen only from \(B,L,d\) so that
\(\|q_s\|_\infty\le2B\) and its Holder constant is at most \(2L\).
The distance map is one-Lipschitz, and for nonnegative \(u,v\),
\[
 |u^\lambda-v^\lambda|\le|u-v|^\lambda.
\tag{8}
\]
Consequently \(f_s=q_s/2\) and \(g_s=-q_s/2\) belong to
\(\mathcal F_{\lambda,L,B}\), agree at all design sites, and differ at
\(z_{0s}\) by \(a\rho_s^\lambda\).  Taking \(z=z_0\) expends zero
testing budget, so
\[
 \Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)\ge aD_X,
 \qquad
 \omega_{s,X}(1;z_{0s})\ge a\rho_s^\lambda.
\tag{9}
\]

For the donor-coordinate lower bound, choose a coordinate direction of one
cohort and a sign pointing into the cube.  Put
\(u_N=\tfrac12(c_\Sigma/N)^{1/2}v\).  For all sufficiently large \(N\),
\(z_0+u_N\) lies in the cube, and
\[
 N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2^2
 \le Nc_\Sigma^{-1}\|u_N\|_2^2=\frac14.
\tag{10}
\]
Choose \(a_0>0\), depending only on \(B,L,d\), so that the one-sided
ridge
\(x\mapsto a_0\{v_s^\top(x-z_{0s})\}_+^\lambda\) belongs to
\(\mathcal F_{\lambda,L,B}\).  Use this same surface as both \(f_s\)
and \(g_s\), use zero surfaces in the other cohorts, and use the displacement
in (10).  The response part of the budget is zero, while the resulting
functional difference is at least \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\).  Hence
\[
 \Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)\ge cN^{-\lambda/2}.
\tag{11}
\]
Equations (5), (9), and (11), together with
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}=A\vee\Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)^2\), yield
\[
 R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)
 \asymp A\vee D_X(z_0)^2\vee N^{-\lambda}.
\tag{12}
\]

Finally suppose \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every \(s\).  Since
\(0<\lambda\le1\), the order convention gives \(r=0\), and the Gram
matrix is scalar.  Its strict positivity at
\((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\), together with the support of \(K\), implies that
some design point satisfies
\(\|X_{st}-z_{0s}\|_2\le h_s^\star\).  Thus
\(\rho_s\le h_s^\star\).  Substitution into (12), followed by the
bandwidth-floor inequality
\[
 (Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d)^{-1/2}\le(h_s^\star)^\lambda,
\]
which follows from
\(h_s^\star\ge(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\), proves
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D\).

proposed.construction:
Fix admissible class constants with \(c_\Sigma\le1/2\),
\(C_\Sigma\ge1\), and \(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\).  Set
\(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_{Sd}\), draw the \(X_{st}\) independently and
uniformly on \([0,1]^d\), and take
\(\Sigma=\tfrac12I_{Sd}+\tfrac{1}{2Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}^{\top}\).
For independent Rademacher vectors \(U_j\in\{-1,1\}^{Sd}\), set
\(Z_j=z_0+\Sigma^{1/2}U_j\).  Put
\(a_0=\min\{B,L,1\}/64\),
\(\bar e=(e_1^{\top},0,\ldots,0)^{\top}\), and
\(q_0=(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}\).  Choose
\(\delta_0\le\min\{1/2,\{2\|\Sigma\bar e/q_0\|_\infty\}^{-1}\}\).
If \(\kappa=1\), set
\(m_1(x)=4a_0+a_0(x_1-1/2)+a_0(x_1-1/2)^2\); if
\(0<\kappa<1\), set
\(m_1(x)=4a_0+a_0(x_1-1/2)_+^{\kappa}-(a_0/2)(1/2-x_1)_+^{\kappa}\);
and set \(m_s(x)=4a_0\) for \(s>1\).  With mutually independent centered
Rademacher noises \(\varepsilon_{sti}\) and \(\eta_{si}\), define
\(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})+a_0\varepsilon_{sti}\),
\(B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_{0s})+a_0\eta_{si}\),
\(B_{si}(1)=B_{si}(0)+a_0\), and
\(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\).  Finally take
\(W_{si,-1}=1\), \(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1\), and
\(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\).  These prescriptions define
\(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\).

proofs.proof_tex:
Set
\[
 a_0=\frac{\min\{B,L,1\}}{64},\qquad
 \bar e=(e_1^{\top},0,\ldots,0)^{\top}\in\mathbb R^{Sd},
 \qquad q_0=(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}.
\]
Because \(B>0\) and \(L>0\), we have \(a_0>0\).  We verify, one condition at a time, that the construction in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} is a member of the class in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}.

First consider the donor law.  By \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp},
\[
 \Sigma=\frac12 I_{Sd}+\frac{1}{2Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}^{\top}.
\]
The eigenvalue in the direction \(\mathbf 1_{Sd}\) is one, and every vector orthogonal to \(\mathbf 1_{Sd}\) has eigenvalue one half.  Hence \(\Sigma\) is positive definite, \(q_0>0\), and the displayed restrictions \(c_\Sigma\le1/2\) and \(C_\Sigma\ge1\) give
\[
 c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}.
\]
This is \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}.  Every off-diagonal entry is \(1/(2Sd)>0\), proving the asserted cross-coordinate and cross-cohort covariance nondegeneracy.

The vectors \((U_j)_{j=1}^{N}\) are independent and identically distributed, \(\mathbb E[U_j]=0\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(U_j)=I_{Sd}\).  The symmetric positive square root used in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} therefore yields
\[
 \mathbb E[Z_j\mid z_0]=z_0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid z_0)
 =\Sigma^{1/2}I_{Sd}\Sigma^{1/2}=\Sigma.
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:donor-independence} and \texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness} hold.  Moreover,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[
   \|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\mid z_0
 \right]
 =\mathbb E[\|U_j\|_2^4]
 =(Sd)^2\le B^4,
\]
which is \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}.

We next check the outcome and causal restrictions.  Both displayed formulas for \(m_1\) give \(m_1(z_{01})=4a_0\), and \(m_s(z_{0s})=4a_0\) for \(s>1\).  Hence
\[
 B_{si}(0)\in\{3a_0,5a_0\},
 \qquad B_{si}(1)\in\{4a_0,6a_0\}.
\]
In particular \(B_{si}(a)>0\), so \(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\), as required by the support of the potential simple return.  Using \texttt{def:buyhold-level}, \(W_{si,-1}=1\), and \(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\),
\[
 W_{si,-1}\prod_{h=0}^{H}\{1+R_{sih}(a)\}
 =1\cdot B_{si}(a)\prod_{h=1}^{H}1
 =B_{si}(a),
\]
where the last product is empty and equals one if \(H=0\).  The prescribed equality \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\) verifies \texttt{ass:consistency}.  Centering and independence of \(\eta_{si}\) give
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]
 =m_s(z_{0s})+a_0\mathbb E[\eta_{si}\mid z_0]
 =m_s(z_{0s}),
\]
which is exactly \texttt{ass:event-date-transport}.

For boundedness, suppose first that \(\kappa=1\) and put \(y=x_1-1/2\).  On \([-1/2,1/2]\),
\[
 -\frac14\le y+y^2\le\frac34,
 \qquad
 \frac{15a_0}{4}\le m_1(x)\le\frac{19a_0}{4}.
\]
If \(0<\kappa<1\), the two one-sided terms cannot be simultaneously nonzero, so
\[
 \frac{7a_0}{2}\le m_1(x)\le5a_0.
\]
All other surfaces equal \(4a_0\).  Since \(\varepsilon_{sti}\) and \(\eta_{si}\) take values in \(\{-1,1\}\), these bounds imply
\[
 |Q_{sti}|\vee |B_{si}(0)|\vee |B_{si}(1)|
 \le6a_0
 \le\frac{6B}{64}<B.
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth} holds, and the noise is genuinely nonzero because
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(Q_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=a_0^2>0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(B_{si}(a)\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=a_0^2>0,
\]
where \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{1\le u\le S,\ 1\le v\le T})\).

We now verify \texttt{ass:holder-regression}.  If \(0<\lambda<1\), then \(\kappa=\lambda\).  For \(v,w\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 |v_+^\lambda-w_+^\lambda|\le |v-w|^\lambda,
 \qquad
 |(-v)_+^\lambda-(-w)_+^\lambda|\le |v-w|^\lambda.
\]
On one side of zero the corresponding one-dimensional cusp therefore has \(\lambda\)-Holder constant at most one.  If \(v\) and \(w\) lie on opposite sides, then
\[
 v_+^\lambda+\frac12(-w)_+^\lambda
 \le\frac32|v-w|^\lambda
\]
after interchanging \(v,w\) if necessary.  Since \(|x_1-x'_1|\le\|x-x'\|_2\), it follows that
\[
 \|m_1\|_\infty+[m_1]_\lambda
 \le5a_0+\frac32a_0
 <7a_0<L.
\]
If \(\lambda\ge1\), the selected surface is quadratic and its only nonzero derivatives of positive order are
\[
 \partial_1m_1(x)=a_0\{1+2(x_1-1/2)\},
 \qquad
 \partial_{11}m_1(x)=2a_0.
\]
The first derivative is bounded by \(2a_0\) and is Lipschitz with constant \(2a_0\); the second derivative is bounded by \(2a_0\); all derivatives of order greater than two vanish.  Under the stated integer-order convention, the isotropic Holder norm is consequently at most \(9a_0<L\) for every \(\lambda\ge1\).  The constant surfaces have norm \(4a_0<L\).  Hence all \(m_s\) belong to \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\).  The first surface is non-affine: it has a nonzero quadratic term when \(\kappa=1\), and an asymmetric cusp when \(0<\kappa<1\).

The \(X_{st}\) are independent and uniform on \([0,1]^d\), so \(f_X(x)=1\).  Since \(c_X\le1\le C_X\), \texttt{ass:design-density} holds.  Also,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(z_{0s},\partial[0,1]^d)=\frac12\ge\delta_0,
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:interior-path}.  Independence across calendar windows implies
\[
 \beta(k)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\qquad(k\ge1),
\]
so \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing} holds.

Conditional on \((z_0,\mathcal X)\), centering and independence of the response noises give
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =m_s(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =m_s(z_{0s})+a_0
 =\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
These are the two equalities in \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}.  The independent arrays \((\varepsilon_{sti})_{s,t,i}\) and \((\eta_{si})_{s,i}\) make the unit histories mutually independent across \((s,i)\) conditional on \((z_0,\mathcal X)\), verifying \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}.  Each \(X_{st}\) is recorded directly, which is \texttt{ass:center-only-design}.

For the clarified \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}, define
\[
 \mathcal Z=\sigma((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}),
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{panel}}
 =\sigma((X_{st},Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i}).
\]
The first field is generated by \((U_j)_{j=1}^{N}\), whereas the second is generated by the mutually independent design, response-noise, and event-noise arrays.  Their product-law construction therefore gives, for every \(A\in\mathcal Z\) and \(C\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{panel}}\),
\[
 \mathbb P(A\cap C\mid z_0)
 =\mathbb P(A\mid z_0)\mathbb P(C\mid z_0).
\]
Thus the donor sample is conditionally independent of the entire joint panel, not merely of its components one at a time.  This proves the clarified separation condition.  We have now verified every member property in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, and hence
\[
 P_{\mathrm{ex}}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}.
\]

It remains to establish the two-sided local-modulus order directly from \texttt{def:local-modulus}.  For \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), put
\[
 u_\delta=\frac{\delta\Sigma\bar e}{q_0}.
\]
Because \(q_0^2=\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e\),
\[
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_\delta\|_2^2
 =\frac{\delta^2}{q_0^2}\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e
 =\delta^2,
 \qquad
 \bar e^{\top}u_\delta=\delta q_0>0.
\]
The radius restriction in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} also gives
\[
 \|u_\delta\|_\infty
 \le\delta_0\|\Sigma\bar e/q_0\|_\infty
 \le\frac12.
\]
Since \(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_{Sd}\), this proves \(z_0+u_\delta\in([0,1]^d)^S\).  Thus \(u_\delta\) is feasible in \texttt{def:local-modulus}.

If \(\kappa=1\), the stacked weighted gradient at \(z_0\) is \(\pi_1a_0\bar e\), and its covariance-standardized dual norm is
\[
 \|\Sigma^{1/2}(\pi_1a_0\bar e)\|_2
 =\pi_1a_0q_0>0.
\]
Substitution of \(u_\delta\) gives the exact increment
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{\delta,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\pi_1a_0(q_0\delta+q_0^2\delta^2)
 =\frac{\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}q_0}{64}\delta+O(\delta^2).
\]
If \(0<\kappa<1\), the positivity of \(\bar e^{\top}u_\delta\) selects the positive cusp branch and yields
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{\delta,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\pi_1a_0q_0^\kappa\delta^\kappa
 =\frac{\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}q_0^\kappa}{64}\delta^\kappa.
\]
Therefore there is a constant \(c_{\mathrm{ex}}>0\), depending only on the fixed displayed parameters, for which
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)
 \ge c_{\mathrm{ex}}\delta^\kappa
 \qquad(0<\delta\le\delta_0).
\]

For the reverse inequality, let \(u\) be any feasible perturbation in \texttt{def:local-modulus}.  The upper ellipticity bound implies
\[
 \|u\|_2
 =\|\Sigma^{1/2}\Sigma^{-1/2}u\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\delta.
\]
Write \(v=\bar e^{\top}u\).  Feasibility of \(z_0+u\) gives \(|v|\le1/2\).  When \(\kappa=1\),
\[
 |m_1(z_{01}+u_1)-m_1(z_{01})|
 =a_0|v+v^2|
 \le\frac32a_0|v|
 \le\frac32a_0C_\Sigma^{1/2}\delta.
\]
When \(0<\kappa<1\), either branch of the asymmetric cusp gives
\[
 |m_1(z_{01}+u_1)-m_1(z_{01})|
 \le a_0|v|^\kappa
 \le a_0C_\Sigma^{\kappa/2}\delta^\kappa.
\]
All other cohort surfaces are constant and \(0<\pi_1\le1\).  Taking the supremum over feasible \(u\), there is a finite constant \(C_{\mathrm{ex}}>0\), depending only on fixed class parameters, such that
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)
 \le C_{\mathrm{ex}}\delta^\kappa
 \qquad(0<\delta\le\delta_0).
\]
Combining the last two displays proves
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\asymp\delta^\kappa
 \qquad\text{as }\delta\downarrow0.
\]
The lower bound was derived for this explicit law and was not assumed for the base Holder class.

Put \(a_0=\min\{B,L,1\}/64\), \(\bar e=(e_1^{\top},0,\ldots,0)^{\top}\), and \(q_0=(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}\). Choose \(\delta_0\le\min\{1/2,\{2\|\Sigma\bar e/q_0\|_\infty\}^{-1}\}\). If \(\kappa=1\), set \(m_1(x)=4a_0+a_0(x_1-1/2)+a_0(x_1-1/2)^2\); if \(0<\kappa<1\), set \(m_1(x)=4a_0+a_0(x_1-1/2)_+^{\kappa}-(a_0/2)(1/2-x_1)_+^{\kappa}\); and set \(m_s(x)=4a_0\) for \(s>1\). proofs.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 \mathcal X=\sigma\!\left((X_{uv})_{1\le u\le S,\,1\le v\le T}\right),
 \qquad
 p_E=\Pr_P(E\mid z_0),
 \qquad
 \mu_{si}=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
Membership of \(P\) in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth}, and \texttt{ass:consistency} imply that \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is integrable.  Since \(E\in\mathcal X\), the random variable \(b\mathbf 1_E\) is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(z_0,\mathcal X)\).  The assumed equality \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b\mathbf 1_E\), valid almost surely under the conditional law given \(z_0\), therefore implies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =b\mathbf 1_E
 \quad\text{almost surely under that conditional law}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
On the other hand, \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]
 =\mu_{si}
 \quad\text{almost surely}.                                                                  \tag{2}
\]
Taking conditional expectation given \(z_0\) in the assumed shock representation gives
\[
 \mu_{si}=b\,\mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1_E\mid z_0]=bp_E.                                           \tag{3}
\]
Combining (1)--(3), squaring, and taking conditional expectation given \(z_0\) yields
\[
 0
 =\mathbb E_P[(b\mathbf 1_E-bp_E)^2\mid z_0]
 =b^2\mathbb E_P[(\mathbf 1_E-p_E)^2\mid z_0]
 =b^2p_E(1-p_E).                                                                              \tag{4}
\]
The last equality uses \(\mathbf 1_E^2=\mathbf 1_E\) and \(\mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1_E\mid z_0]=p_E\).  Because \(b\ne0\), division by \(b^2\) in (4) gives \(p_E(1-p_E)=0\).  Since a conditional probability lies in \([0,1]\),
\[
 \Pr_P(E\mid z_0)=p_E\in\{0,1\}.
\]

For the former scalar construction in the statement, \(z_0\) is fixed, \(X_{11}\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), \(E=\{X_{11}\le q\}\), and \(q\in(0,1)\).  Hence
\[
 \Pr_P(E\mid z_0)=\Pr_P(X_{11}\le q\mid z_0)=q\in(0,1).
\]
Taking \(b=b_*>0\) contradicts (4).  Thus the shocked law violates \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}; by the member-property construction in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, it is not an element of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  The former obstruction required the shocked law to belong to that class, so that obstruction is excluded.  This argument uses the observed-law centering restriction and does not invoke causal event-date transport.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), a cohort \(s\), and a unit \(i\), and put
\[
 \mu_{si}=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
Membership, \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth}, and \texttt{ass:consistency} make this conditional mean finite.  By \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering},
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=0.                            \tag{5}
\]
Let \(W\) be bounded and \(\mathcal X\)-measurable.  Then \((B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si})W\) is integrable, and \(W\) is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(z_0,\mathcal X)\).  The pull-out and tower properties of conditional expectation applied to (5) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P[(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si})W\mid z_0]
 &=\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 W\,\mathbb E_P(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 \mathrel{\Big|}z_0\right]\\
 &=0.
\end{aligned}                                                                                \tag{6}
\]
This is the asserted conditional orthogonality.

Now take \(E\in\mathcal X\) and write \(p_E=\Pr_P(E\mid z_0)\).  Substituting \(W=\mathbf 1_E\) into (6) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mathbf 1_E\mid z_0]=\mu_{si}p_E.                          \tag{7}
\]
If \(p_E>0\), division of (7) by \(p_E\), using the definition of conditional expectation on an event, yields
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E]=\mu_{si}.                                     \tag{8}
\]
Applying the same argument to \(E^c\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E^c]=\mu_{si}                                    \tag{9}
\]
whenever \(p_E<1\).  Thus (8)--(9) hold simultaneously if \(0<p_E<1\).  The exclusion of the former common-design-shock experiment is exactly \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction}.

It remains to prove that this centering repair does not itself fix the centered event-noise constant.  For every positive \(N,T,n_1\), choose the admissible scalar fixed parameters
\[
 S=1,
 \quad \pi_1=1,
 \quad H=0,
 \quad p=d=1,
 \quad z_0=\frac12,
 \quad \lambda=\kappa=1,
 \quad B=L=1,
 \quad \delta_0=\frac14,
\]
and set \(c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), with arbitrary fixed \(\beta_0>0\) and \(\rho_0\in(0,1)\).  The identity \(d=p(H+1)=1\) and all displayed parameter ranges are satisfied.

On a product probability space, let \((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T}\), \((\xi_j)_{j=1}^{N}\), and \((\varepsilon_i)_{i=1}^{n_1}\) be mutually independent, with
\[
 X_{1t}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[0,1],
 \qquad
 \Pr(\xi_j=1)=\Pr(\xi_j=-1)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \Pr(\varepsilon_i=1)=\Pr(\varepsilon_i=-1)=\frac12.
\]
Define the untreated regression, training responses, and donor scores by
\[
 m_1(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Q_{1ti}=m_1(X_{1t})=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Z_j=\frac12+\xi_j.                                                                          \tag{10}
\]
For every event unit put \(W_{1i,-1}=1/2\) and \(R_{1i0}(0)=0\).  By \texttt{def:buyhold-level},
\[
 B_{1i}(0)=\frac12.                                                                           \tag{11}
\]
Under \(P^{(0)}\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=0\).  Under \(P^{(1)}\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=\varepsilon_i/2\).  In both laws impose \texttt{ass:consistency} by defining \(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{1i}(1)\).  The buy-and-hold formula then gives
\[
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\frac12
 \quad\text{under }P^{(0)},
 \qquad
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\frac12+\frac14\varepsilon_i
 \quad\text{under }P^{(1)}.                                                                  \tag{12}
\]
All constructed returns lie in \((-1,\infty)\), because the smallest possible return is \(-1/2\).

We verify every member property of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}\).  Equations (10)--(12) give
\[
 |Q_{1ti}|=\frac12,
 \qquad
 |B_{1i}(0)|=\frac12,
 \qquad
 |B_{1i}(1)|\le\frac34,
\]
so \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth} holds with \(B=1\).  The constant \(m_1\) has supremum norm \(1/2\), every positive-order derivative equal to zero, and Holder seminorm zero.  Hence \(m_1\in\mathcal H_1(1,1)\), as required by \texttt{ass:holder-regression}.  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}\!\left(\frac12,\partial[0,1]\right)=\frac12\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad
 f_X(x)=1\quad(0\le x\le1),                                                                  \tag{13}
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:interior-path} and \texttt{ass:design-density}.

Conditional on the complete design array, every training outcome in (10) is deterministic.  Under \(P^{(0)}\), the event outcomes are deterministic; under \(P^{(1)}\), unit \(i\)'s event history depends only on \(\varepsilon_i\).  Independence of the \(\varepsilon_i\)'s therefore proves \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} while leaving no restriction beyond the stated conditional independence across units.  The calendar blocks in (10) are independent over \(t\), so their beta-mixing coefficients satisfy
\[
 \beta(k)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k\ge1,                                                                               \tag{14}
\]
which proves \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.  Declaring each \(X_{1t}\) in (10) directly observed verifies \texttt{ass:center-only-design}.

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T})\).  Equation (10) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Q_{1ti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\frac12
 =m_1(X_{1t}).                                                                                \tag{15}
\]
Under either law, (12), independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from \(\mathcal X\), and \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i]=0\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\frac12
 =\mathbb E_P[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].                                               \tag{16}
\]
Thus both clauses of \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} hold.

For the clarified donor-versus-joint-panel factorization, define
\[
 \mathcal D=\sigma((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}),
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{pan}}
 =\sigma((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T},(Q_{1ti})_{t,i},(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i=1}^{n_1}).
\]
By (10), every \(Q_{1ti}\) is measurable with respect to \(\mathcal X\), while by (12) every event outcome is either constant or measurable with respect to \(\sigma((\varepsilon_i)_{i=1}^{n_1})\).  Hence \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{pan}}\subseteq\sigma((X_{1t})_t,(\varepsilon_i)_i)\).  Conversely, \(\mathcal D\subseteq\sigma((\xi_j)_j)\).  Mutual independence of the three primitive arrays therefore yields
\[
 \mathcal D\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}\mathcal P_{\mathrm{pan}}\mid z_0,                  \tag{17}
\]
where conditioning on \(z_0=1/2\) is conditioning on a constant.  Equation (17) is exactly the clarified \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}; it factors the donors from the entire joint panel and places no additional restriction on dependence within a unit history.

By (10), conditional on the fixed \(z_0=1/2\), the donor scores are independent and identically distributed and satisfy
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Z_j\mid z_0]=z_0,
 \qquad
 \Sigma=\operatorname{Var}_P(Z_j\mid z_0)=1.                                                 \tag{18}
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:donor-independence} and \texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness} hold.  Since \(c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), (18) proves \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}.  Finally,
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 |\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4\mid z_0
 \right]
 =\mathbb E[|\xi_j|^4]
 =1
 =B^4,                                                                                        \tag{19}
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment} while retaining the full scalar covariance.

Equation (11) and the definition of \(m_1\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]
 =\frac12
 =m_1(z_0),                                                                                  \tag{20}
\]
so \texttt{ass:event-date-transport} holds.  Consistency was imposed before (12).  We have therefore verified every member property listed in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, and hence
\[
 P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}.
\]
In particular, neither law uses a class-wide lower local-modulus condition.

The joint law of \(((X_{1t})_t,(Q_{1ti})_{t,i},(Z_j)_j)\) is the same under \(P^{(0)}\) and \(P^{(1)}\) by (10) and the common product construction.  By \texttt{def:target}, (11)--(12), and the zero mean of a Rademacher variable,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \tau_{P^{(0)}}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{P^{(0)}}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]=0,\\
 \tau_{P^{(1)}}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{P^{(1)}}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]
 =\frac14\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i]=0.
\end{aligned}                                                                                \tag{21}
\]
Nevertheless, (12) and independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from \(\mathcal X\) yield
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(0)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(1)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 =\frac1{16}\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i)
 =\frac1{16}.                                                                                \tag{22}
\]
Thus the centered class permits both event-noise constants while holding the training experiment, donor experiment, and causal target fixed.  Equations (5)--(9) prove the asserted orthogonality and eventwise mean invariance, while (10)--(22) give the explicit two-law certificate under the clarified donor-versus-joint-panel factorization.  Therefore excluding the invalid common-design-shock witness is logically distinct from calculating a sharp minimax constant for the remaining centered product experiment.

proposed.condition:
The conditional independence
\[
